info.name: DeliGo Ride-Sharing API
info.description:
Complete, production-grade Postman collection for DeliGo Ride-Sharing platform backend.

### Authentication & Authorization
All protected endpoints (REST and Socket.IO) require a JWT: send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`, `Bearer {{driverAccessToken}}`, `Bearer {{fleetAccessToken}}` (fleet manager) or `Bearer {{adminAccessToken}}`. For Socket.IO pass the same token as `auth.token` in the handshake (or the `Authorization` header).
   - Customer/Driver/Admin login and OTP verification endpoints automatically extract and populate these collection variables.
   - The legacy `x-mock-user-id` / `x-mock-role` headers are no longer supported.

### Refresh tokens (platform-aware)
The refresh token is always set as an httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie (path `/api/v1/auth`).
- **Web / portals (default, admin + fleet):** the token is delivered ONLY as the cookie; JSON has `tokens: {accessToken, expiresIn}`. Postman's cookie jar resends it automatically.
- **Mobile apps:** send `x-client-platform: mobile` (or `x-platform: android|ios`, or `"includeRefreshToken": true` in the body). The JSON then also contains `tokens.refreshToken`, captured into `{{refreshToken}}`, for storage in SecureStore / Keychain.
- `POST /auth/refresh-token` and `POST /auth/logout` accept the refresh token from the cookie OR the JSON body.

### Routes & roles
There is no `/admin` URL prefix. Every module is mounted once (`/users`, `/rides`, `/support`, ...) and each request is labelled with its role in the request description. List/detail endpoints such as `GET /rides` and `GET /support/tickets` are role-scoped: customers and drivers only see their own data, admins see everything.

### Automatic Variable Extraction
All authentication and creation endpoints automatically capture IDs and tokens (such as `accessToken`, `driverAccessToken`, `adminAccessToken`, `refreshToken` (mobile only), `signupSessionId`, `adminInviteToken`, `activeRideId`, `activeVehicleId`, `activeTicketId`, `activePromoId`, `activeAlertId`) and populate Collection Variables for chained testing workflows.

item.name: Session & Tokens
item.description: Silent refresh rotation and session termination.

header.description: Mobile apps receive refreshToken in the JSON body as well as the cookie

request.description:
Rotates the session using the httpOnly `refreshToken` cookie that login / verify-otp / social login set (Postman's cookie jar sends it automatically). The refresh token is NO LONGER returned in the JSON body. A legacy `refreshToken` body field is still read by the server if sent. Returns `data.tokens.{accessToken, expiresIn}`; the rotated refresh token is set as a new cookie. Enforces token-family reuse detection.

(Public. Path: /auth/refresh-token)

Platform: MOBILE. Sends `x-client-platform: mobile`, so `data.tokens.refreshToken` is returned in the JSON body (in addition to the httpOnly cookie) and captured into `{{refreshToken}}`. Web clients omit the header and receive the cookie only.

header.description: Mobile apps receive refreshToken in the JSON body as well as the cookie

request.description:
Revokes the active session, blacklists the JTI in Redis, and clears the refreshToken HTTP-only cookie.

Platform: MOBILE. Sends `x-client-platform: mobile`, so `data.tokens.refreshToken` is returned in the JSON body (in addition to the httpOnly cookie) and captured into `{{refreshToken}}`. Web clients omit the header and receive the cookie only.

Also clears the user's FCM push token so a signed-out device stops receiving pushes. Optional body fields: `fcmToken` (clear only this device's token) and `clearFcmToken: false` (keep the token). `refreshToken` may come from the cookie or the body.
